domain: AI Powered Engineering Upskilling Program - Help Desk

faqs.a: It is a 10-module program that takes you from Python basics to deploying real AI applications: data analysis, machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, NLP, generative AI, agents, deployment, and a final capstone.
Just curiosity and basic computer skills. Module 1 starts from Python fundamentals, so no prior programming experience is required.

faqs.q: Which programming language does the course use?
faqs.a: Python. It is the most popular language for AI and data science, and every module uses it.
The syllabus is about 50 hours of content across 10 modules, but you can go at your own pace.

faqs.q: What tools do I need to install?
faqs.a: Python and an editor like VS Code. Later modules use libraries such as NumPy, Pandas, scikit-learn, Flask, and Streamlit, which you install with pip.
Machine learning is teaching a computer to find patterns in data and make predictions, instead of writing the rules by hand. Module 4 covers it in depth.

faqs.q: What is the difference between AI and machine learning?
faqs.a: AI is the broad goal of making machines act intelligently. Machine learning is one way to get there, by learning patterns from data. Deep learning is a subset of machine learning that uses neural networks.

faqs.q: How do I deploy my model?
faqs.a: Save the trained model to a file, load it inside a web app built with Flask or Streamlit, and host it on a free platform like Streamlit Community Cloud or Render. Module 9 walks through this.
The final module where you build one complete, end-to-end AI solution - such as a chatbot, a resume analyzer, or a medical assistant - and present it as your portfolio centerpiece.
Yes. Completing all 10 modules earns you the AI Powered Engineering Upskilling Program certificate, which you can add to your resume and LinkedIn.

faqs.q: What careers can this lead to?
faqs.a: Roles like Data Analyst, Data Scientist, Machine Learning Engineer, and AI/LLM Engineer. Module 9 covers career paths in detail.

faqs.q: What is a large language model?
faqs.a: A large language model (LLM) is an AI trained on huge amounts of text that predicts the next word to generate human-like language. Module 7 covers LLMs and prompt engineering.
This is a demo chatbot, so there is no live support. In a real product, this answer would include an email address or a link to a help desk.
